about: Urdu words AI voices say wrong, and the spelling that fixes each. Every entry came from a real take that went wrong. check_takes.py uses the regexes under 'heard' to tell a good take from a bad one; lint_script.py uses 'find' to warn before any audio is made.
source: Unless a rule says otherwise, every rule was heard with one OmniVoice voice clone (2026-10). Other engines guess vowels the same way, but not always on the same words.

rules.why: Without the pesh the voice reads 'khafiya'. With it, takes say 'khufiya'. ذاتی is a safe alternative.
PIN written without a zer is read 'pan'.
The alif in اسٹیپ turns 'two step' into 'two steep'.
'Click' comes out as 'kil'. Write around it; Urdu has good words for the action.
The voice never makes the hard ڈ here, in every spelling tried (Urdu, Latin, ARPAbet). Write شعبہ instead, or warn the person first.
چھن is read 'chhan'. چھین carries the ی and can't be misread.
Heard as 'sufa'. Most people say پیج anyway. It changes the register, so offer it to the person rather than applying it silently.
The joined form runs together. Two words read cleanly.
Spelling doesn't fix this one; takes vary. Check every take: English must hear 'WhatsApp' as many times as the script says it, and Devanagari must not show आप.
Usually fine. Never put a comma between سائبر and سیکیورٹی: it makes a pause.

latin_letters.why: Latin letters inside Urdu text are read unpredictably. Spell acronyms and English words in Urdu letters.

numbers.why: Engines read digits in Urdu unreliably, and words also set the register. Write numbers, dates, times and amounts as words. For example 15 مارچ 2026 becomes پندرہ مارچ، دو ہزار چھبیس, and Rs. 500 becomes پانچ سو روپے.

honorifics.why: Honorific signs are special characters that engines may skip silently. Write them out in full, in the organisation's own form. The form of ؑ ؓ ؒ depends on who is meant (عنہ for a man, عنہا for a woman, عنہم for a group), so --fix leaves those for a person.

signs.ؓ: رضی اللہ عنہ / عنہا / عنہم / عنہما

polite_imperatives.why: A final ں drops at a pause: دیں came out as دی, نہ دیں as ندی. The polite forms don't have the problem and sound more respectful.

weak_endings.why: A paragraph's last consonant gets swallowed (گائیڈ came out as گائب). Keep these words away from the very end of a paragraph, or check that the ending is heard.
